story_type: Coast Guard advanced helicopter rescue school, swimmers hoisted over big surf and against cliffs, training
hook: Dangling over Pacific surf on purpose.
narration: This rescue swimmer is dangling over Pacific surf on purpose.
This is the Coast Guard's Advanced Helicopter Rescue School, on the Oregon and Washington coast.
Crews train here in fall and spring, when Pacific Northwest storms bring high seas and big surf.
Swimmers practice getting survivors out of the surf zone and up to the helicopter.
The pilot can't see straight down, so the flight mechanic leans out the door and talks the pilot over the swimmer.
They train for cliff rescues too, lowering a swimmer right down against the rock.
Then the cable reels in, and the swimmer swings back up under the rotor.
outcome: The swimmer rode the cable back up to the helicopter, and that run in the surf was done.
